result:
I found 12 rules where the code didn't match its docstring and fixed all of them in `pricebook.py`.

| Rule | What it did wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | Rounded the discount with `round()` | Rounds down to the won (`//`) |
| 45 | Capped the price instead of the discount | Calculates the discount first, then caps it at 10,000 won |
| 46 | Started at 101+ units instead of 100+ (`qty > 100`) | `qty >= 100` |
| 47 | Started at 51+ units instead of 50+ (`qty > 50`) | `qty >= 50` |
| 69 | Gave 13% instead of 12% | 12% |
| 90 | Capped the price instead of the discount | Caps the discount at 100,000 won |
| 100 | A whole rule that only discounted units above the threshold | Discounts all units |
| 114 | Only capped the discount when it went over 200,000 won | Always caps it at 100,000 won |
| 123 | Started at 101+ units instead of 100+ (`qty > 100`) | `qty >= 100` |
| 136 | A whole rule that only discounted units above the threshold | Discounts all units |
| 144 | A marginal rule that discounted all units | Discounts only units above 20 |
| 150 | Capped the price instead of the discount | Caps the discount at 10,000 won |

**Check:** after all the edits, I ran one script that builds the expected price from each of the 150 docstrings. It compared that against each rule over a range of quantities, including the edge cases just below and at each threshold, and several unit prices. There were no mismatches.

STATUS: DONE
